record.summary: Designates the Digital Trust Centre, a national centre hosted at Nanyang Technological University, as Singapore's AI Safety Institute. The AISI drives Singapore's AI evaluation and testing work to help address gaps in global AI safety science. IMDA is the overall government agency for it, responsible for baseline policy and international engagement, while the Centre does the technical work. Its work covers technical testing, including multilingual and agentic AI testing and joint testing with international partners, studies of AI's societal impact such as emotional dependency, and international partnerships, including capacity building in ASEAN.
record.notes: IMDA's factsheet announcing the designation carries the dateline Singapore, 22 May 2024; IMDA last updated the page on 10 Oct 2024. IMDA partners the Digital Trust Centre to drive the AISI's technical work. The Centre is funded by a $50 million grant from the National Research Foundation and IMDA, starting from 1 Oct 2022. The AISI's joint testing is done with other members of the international Network for Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science (NAAIMES).

issuing_body.quote: Digital Trust Centre designated as Singapore's AISI | IMDA

As the designated Singapore AISI, the Digital Trust Centre Singapore (DTC), in partnership with the Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore (IMDA), will drive the efforts for advancing AI safety in Singapore.
Hosted in the Nanyang Technological University (NTU), the Digital Trust Centre is a national centre that leads Singapore's research and development efforts in trust technologies, including AI safety.

summary.quote: The Singapore AI Safety Institute (AISI) will drive Singapore's AI evaluation and testing work, to support addressing gaps in global AI safety sciences.

IMDA is the overall government agency for the Singapore AISI, responsible for developing baseline policy, as well as fronting international engagements and partnerships related to AI safety with other AISIs and government agencies.
IMDA also partners the Digital Trust Centre (DTC) to drive the technical work for the Singapore AISI.
Our testing work includes bilateral and joint testing efforts with other members of the international Network for Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science (NAAIMES)
Agentic AI testing: As AI systems become more autonomous and goal-directed, we study how agentic behaviours emerge and scale
Our work examines issues such as emotional dependency and cognitive offloading
Regionally, we work closely with partners in ASEAN and Asia-Pacific to build capacity in testing

safety_topics.quote: Multilingual, multicultural testing: To ensure AI works reliably, fairly and safely across languages, norms and lived experiences.
Internationally, we collaborate on joint testing exercises with members of NAAIMES
